title: TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX: The Lethal Breath-Stealer
summary: A life-threatening, time-sensitive emergency characterized by progressive accumulation of air in the pleural space, leading to hemodynamic collapse via obstructive shock. Immediate clinical diagnosis and decompression are mandatory.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Mechanism
sections.content: Tension pneumothorax is the presence of air in the pleural space with a 'one-way valve' mechanism. Air enters during inspiration but cannot exit during expiration. This results in positive intrapleural pressure, mediastinal shift, compression of the contralateral lung, and decreased venous return to the heart (obstructive shock).

sections.title: Pathophysiology Flow
content: Step 1: Pleural defect allows unidirectional airflow (valvular mechanism).
Step 2: Progressive intrapleural pressure elevation exceeds atmospheric pressure.
Step 3: Mediastinal deviation to the contralateral side.
Step 4: Mechanical obstruction of the Superior/Inferior Vena Cava.
Step 5: Drop in Preload -> Reduced Cardiac Output -> Obstructive Shock -> Cardiac Arrest.

sections.title: Red Flags: Immediate Action Required
content: Unilateral absent breath sounds
Tracheal deviation (Late sign!)
Distended neck veins (JVD)
Hypotension/Hemodynamic instability
Severe, rapid-onset dyspnea
Cyanosis and altered mental status

sections.title: Emergency Management Protocol
content: Step 1: Clinical Diagnosis ONLY (Do not wait for CXR!)
Step 2: Immediate Needle Decompression (14-16G needle)
Step 3: Location: 2nd Intercostal Space (Mid-clavicular) OR 4th/5th ICS (Mid-axillary)
Step 4: Emergent Tube Thoracostomy (Chest Tube, 28-32 French)
Step 5: Connect to underwater seal suction (-20 cm H2O)

sections.title: Diagnostic Pearls
content: Percussion: Hyper-resonance to percussion
Auscultation: Silent hemithorax
Imaging: If stable, CXR shows deep sulcus sign/mediastinal shift
POCUS: Lung point and absent lung sliding are diagnostic

content.explanation: P: Pleural air (trapped), D: Distended veins (JVD), T: Tracheal shift, H: Hypotension/Hypoxia
